name: Water on Jezero's western rim
objective: Walk from a flat camp on Jezero crater's western rim to outcrops where orbital spectra show minerals formed or altered by water: Fe/Mg clays and olivine with carbonate. Compare them with nearby pyroxene-rich rock, whose spectra show no alteration minerals, and finish with a panorama from the rim's high point.
basis: Each outcrop is placed on a patch of CRISM mineral detections in included-data/Jezero_WesternRim_Minerals_CRISM.tif (positions accurate to about 28–75 m). The camp is the nearest ground with no slope steeper than 4° within 120 m in the CTX elevation model. The viewpoint is the highest elevation within 2 km of the centre of the outcrop cluster. Every leg was checked to be reachable under all three route slope limits.

targets.name: Rim camp
targets.detail: Flat ground chosen from the elevation data: no slope steeper than 4° within 120 m.

targets.name: Clay outcrop
targets.detail: CRISM detects Fe/Mg phyllosilicates here: clay minerals that form when water alters rock.

targets.name: Pyroxene outcrop
targets.detail: CRISM detects pyroxene-rich rock about 220 m from the clays. Compare it with the altered rock nearby.

targets.name: Olivine–carbonate outcrop
targets.detail: CRISM detects strong olivine with carbonate here. Carbonate can form when water reacts with olivine and can preserve signs of past environments.

targets.name: Weak olivine exposure
targets.detail: CRISM detects a weaker olivine signature: a contrast to the stronger olivine–carbonate outcrop to the south.

targets.name: Rim viewpoint
targets.detail: Highest point in the elevation data within 2 km of the outcrop cluster: a panorama across the rim and down into the crater.
